gm_decisions.ruling_narrative: Labor's automatic-enforcement demand already locked by USTR this round—duplicate denied.

_reactions.ustr: Okay—we're close, but Congress and supply-chain just flagged the same gap: once the labor panel finds a violation, what *actually happens*? Mexico covers the cost, we suspend sourcing, tariffs kick in? And the six-year review—is that a hard reboot or a consultation? I need those two lines locked in treaty language *this round*, or we're signing Monday on a framework that ratification torches in September.
_reactions.canada_min: USTR, on the six-year hard reboot — does that mean automatic renegotiation of the whole agreement, or just the auto/labor provisions? Because my manufacturers need to know if they're building tooling for a six-year window or if there's real stability built in past that.
_reactions.mexico_neg: Alright, USTR's scope is clear—labor and autos renegotiate in year six, everything else stays locked. That's the stability my members need. Monday we sign all three countries, treaty text in hand, no side letters, no implementation discretion. Canada, your tooling window is protected. Let's initial.
_reactions.us_congress: Look, I'm ready to move this to ratification — but Congress won't touch it unless the treaty text spells out exactly what happens when the panel finds a violation. Not "appropriate measures," not "may suspend sourcing" — *binding, automatic consequence* tied to the violation. Mexico just said tariffs on that supplier's goods suspend until corrected; that's the language we put in the treaty, right? Because if USTR's writing that detail in regulations after we sign, my members kill this in committee, and we lose the whole deal.
_reactions.auto_industry: Mexico's tariff-suspension language on willful violation—that's concrete, I can sell that to my members. But I need one line in the treaty: does the panel's finding of non-compliance *automatically* suspend sourcing on that supplier's goods, or does USTR decide case-by-case? Because if it's discretionary, we're back to uncertainty. Auto and labor renegotiate in year six, everything else locked—that's the stability we need. If that's in treaty text Monday, we're ready to commit the retooling.
_reactions.dairy_ag: Canada, one final thing before Monday—the 3.6% dairy access, that's in the treaty schedule as a binding commitment, not a side letter or voluntary pledge, right? My members need to know it survives ratification and can't be walked back. Once I hear that's locked in the text, we're done.
_reactions.supply_chain_mfr: USTR, one final line: when the panel finds willful violation, the treaty text says tariffs *automatically* suspend on that supplier's goods until corrected—not "may suspend," not USTR's discretion. That language Monday, and I'm telling my members we can commit the retooling. That the actual treaty language?
